input.quote: Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Paragraph (h) is the only assignment provision and there is no change-of-control trigger anywhere in the Agreement, so Kubient has no termination or re-pricing right on our change of control. Customer already has the preferred affiliate and successor carve-out and a reasonableness standard on consent. However, the same no-consent carve-out runs to Kubient, so Kubient can assign to any affiliate, asset purchaser or merger successor without our consent, and nothing prevents assignment to a Customer competitor. That mutual no-consent exception also conflicts with the fallback requirement that all non-successor assignments require consent, so the clause fails both levels on a material term. We have made the affiliate/asset-purchaser/successor carve-out Customer-only and barred assignment by Kubient to a competitor of Customer, leaving the balance of paragraph (h) verbatim.

proposal.summary: Limit the no-consent affiliate/successor exception to Customer and bar Kubient from assigning to a Customer competitor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made the no-consent affiliate and successor carve-out available to Customer only, so Kubient's assignments continue to require our consent (not unreasonably withheld), and added a bar on assignment to a Customer competitor.
